subject: Custom SLA addendum & order form language — uptime/latency mitigations
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@medsyn.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Draft SLA addendum + order form language for Medsyn integration

Daniel —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, attached is a first-pass SLA addendum and a short order form extract with the specific uptime/latency commitments we can offer for the Dedicated plan we scoped. Highlights:

- 99.95% Monthly Availability (standard)
- Target p50/p95 request latency guidance on our hosted endpoints; Dedicated customers can request tailored latency SLOs with capacity commitments
- Scheduled maintenance windows called out, with notice and excluded downtime calculation
- Service credits table and exclusion for customer-caused outages

Two things I want to flag up-front that Medsyn asked about: the handling of burst traffic (burst windows during batch ingest of clinical records) and whether we can provide an explicit latency exception carve-out during scheduled onboarding runs. Karthik and I sketched two possible clauses in the attached: one that allows temporary relaxed p95 targets during pre-agreed ramp windows, and another that limits credits for capacity-related degradation when usage spikes exceed agreed baseline throughput.

Please review and let me know the parts you want refined. If you prefer, we can redline and send back for legal review; alternatively, we can do a short call next week to walk through the language.

Attachments: Medsyn_Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf; Redwood_OrderForm_Draft_20270210.docx

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192


From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@medsyn.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medsyn.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA addendum + order form language for Medsyn integration

Priya —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear draft. A couple of immediate concerns from procurement/infra:

1) Burst handling: we run nightly bulk ingest and sometimes a few large batches a month for analytics. We need a committed behavior rather than a carve-out that shifts risk to us. Can Redwood commit to an agreed burst capacity (either X concurrent tokens or Y RPS) for the first 90 days post-onboarding? If not, we need stronger language around credits.

2) Latency SLO: Medsyn needs a p95 <= 250ms for standard API calls for clinical inference use cases. I realize that might be aggressive; please confirm whether this is achievable on Dedicated, and if not, propose a realistic p95 with the corresponding throughput requirement.

3) Maintenance windows: procurement wants a max 4-hour monthly scheduled window and at least 7 days notice; any emergency maintenance should be logged and notified within 1 hour.

If we can get concrete numbers for burst capacity and a proposed p95/throughput mapping, procurement can move forward with redlines.

Thanks,
Daniel Reyes
Head of Procurement
Medsyn Health
Daniel.Reyes@medsyn.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@medsyn.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA addendum + order form language for Medsyn integration

Daniel —

Thanks for the detailed asks. Quick internal summary of feasibility and proposed language:

- Burst capacity: We can offer a tiered burst commitment for the first 90 days post-onboarding. Proposal: baseline throughput X = 200 RPS (sustained), with a burst allowance up to 600 RPS for discrete 10-minute windows, 10 such windows per month. We'd surface this as an appendix to the Order Form ("Burst Capacity Schedule").

- Latency SLO: On Dedicated with the baseline X above and appropriate model selection (configurable quantization and batching), we can commit to p95 <= 300ms at baseline. To reach p95 <= 250ms we need either 30% higher baseline GPU reservation or a higher-priced priority lane. We propose two options in the attached revised addendum: Option A (p95 <= 300ms at baseline X), Option B (p95 <= 250ms with Priority Lane + baseline X * 1.3).

- Maintenance windows: We can agree to a max 4-hour scheduled monthly window with >=7 days notice. Emergency maintenance will be limited and notified within 1 hour; we will provide an incident summary within 24 hours.

- Credits: For availability < committed %, same tiered credits table in the draft applies. For burst-related degradation within the defined Burst Capacity Schedule, credits are capped to 25% of the standard credit for availability breaches (to avoid double-dipping).

I'll attach a tracked-changes addendum with the specific wording for the Burst Capacity Schedule and the two latency options. Priya — if this looks good to you, send to Daniel with the tracked changes and ask procurement which latency option they prefer.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@medsyn.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA addendum + order form language for Medsyn integration

Daniel —

Attached is the redline (tracked_changes_addendum.docx) incorporating Karthik's burst schedule and the two latency options. Summary:

- We added an appendix named "Burst Capacity Schedule" with explicit ceilings and windows.
- Two latency options are presented; procurement should choose A (no price change) or B (Priority Lane, +30% baseline reservation).
- Maintenance and notification language updated to 7 days notice and 1-hour emergency notification with 24-hour incident summary.

Next steps: please confirm which latency option you prefer and whether procurement is comfortable with the burst windows as written. Once we have that, we can prepare an Order Form that lists the selected option and a DocuSign packet for signature.

Attachments: tracked_changes_addendum.docx; Medsyn_Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Priya

From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@medsyn.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medsyn.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA addendum + order form language for Medsyn integration

Priya, Karthik —

This is helpful and much closer to what procurement needs. A couple of small asks before we sign:

1) For the Burst Capacity Schedule, replace the "10 windows per month" with "10 windows per billing cycle" to align to our fiscal cadence.
2) Procurement prefers Option B (p95 <= 250ms) but requests a 45-day implementation window after signature to allow capacity provisioning and validation.

If Redwood can accept (1) and (2) we'll route the redline through legal today and expect to countersign. Also, please generate the DocuSign packet with Option B selected and the implementation timeline noted.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Daniel
